title: Decision: a registered client's PING is answered through the agent, not from the socket
description:
Mark, 2026-11-27: 'can i want the pong to come out of the mimi process instead of the irc process? the whole point of ping pong is "are you working"'.

BEFORE. mimid-agent-irc answered a client's PING in register.rs:185 by formatting ':server PONG server :token' and writing it, touching nothing of the agent. A PONG proved the connection task was pumping lines. It did not prove the store was reachable or the sync loop alive, so an agent wedged on the agent lock still told every irssi that it was working. PING was the one command on the connection that answered while every other command -- JOIN, PRIVMSG, MODE -- would have blocked on the same lock.

MIMI DEFINES NO KEEPALIVE. draft-ietf-mimi-protocol-07, content-10, arch-03, room-policy-04 and mls-extensions-11 contain no ping, pong, keepalive, heartbeat or liveness: agent and provider speak request/response over HTTPS. The keepalives mimid has are the bindings' own (IRC's PING, JMAP EventSource's ping events, RFC 8620 7.3; the live stream has none). So there is no MIMI-level probe to carry, and what a PONG can be backed by is local evidence only.

CHOSEN. For a registered session, the PONG is written only after the connection task has held the agent lock: the same lock the user's next PRIVMSG needs. A PONG then means 'I could have taken your message', not 'the socket is open'. An unregistered connection keeps the plain immediate answer, so an unauthenticated peer still cannot queue work behind the agent.

NOT CHOSEN: withholding PONG when the provider is unreachable. That would invent a liveness semantic MIMI does not define, and an agent whose provider is down still serves history and queues sends in the outbox, so dropping the client would be wrong. A provider that cannot be reached is reported through the mimid service nick instead.

NOT DECIDED HERE: a sync loop that has panicked frees the lock, so a PONG is still written. Nothing in mimid-agent-store reports a loop that exited (runner.rs: 'Nothing here watches the state lock or takes an account over'). That is its own question.

COST. During a long but healthy sync the PONG is delayed with everything else on that connection, and a client whose ping timeout is shorter than the sync gives up and reconnects. agent-frontends.md 4 already warned that 'a client with a short ping timeout may give up during a long sync'; that is now the intended signal rather than an accident, and the invented 90 s + 90 s the daemon itself uses are unchanged.
notes:
EXTENDED 2026-11-27, Mark: 'well, also make sure the jmap and hte binary pingpong are wired in'.

JMAP, BOTH ENDS. The EventSource ping (RFC 8620 7.3) was written by the stream task's timer at each interval, touching nothing behind it.
- The provider (mimid-server jmap/eventsource.rs) now reads the account's states first, exactly as a change does, and sends nothing if that read fails: the stream ends with the same jmap_eventsource_state_failed a change logs and the client opens it again. The values are discarded; a state event is the change's to send.
- The agent (mimid-agent http.rs) takes the agent lock with try_lock and skips the ping while it is held, rather than parking: a skipped ping is one the client tolerates (its own read timeout allows several intervals), the task stays able to notice a closed stream and a shutdown, and an agent that never frees the lock writes no further ping, which is what the read timeout is for.

THE LIVE STREAM HAS NOTHING TO WIRE. mimid's own binding defines no keepalive in either direction, nothing in mimid sends a WebSocket Ping, and a Ping that arrives was already answered inside tungstenite before any mimid code saw it. Recorded in binary-live-stream.md 4 and held open as bead mimid-j729, which needs a decision: a transport Ping answers 'is the pipe there', an application-level probe answers 'can the provider serve', and they are different questions.

MIMI HAS NO KEEPALIVE TO BORROW, so every constant here is mimid's own. Bead mimid-f9x4 drafts what a MIMI keepalive would have to say; not sent.

TESTED. The negative property -- the answer is withheld while the thing behind it is wedged -- is asserted on IRC only (a_ping_is_answered_once_the_agent_is_free), where a second connection's CAP LIST is a sound witness that the daemon is serving while the first connection's PING waits. For the two EventSource pings there is no knob for the interval and MIN_PING_SECS is 10 s, so a negative assertion would need a sleep past that window and could not tell a withheld ping from a slow machine. What is tested there is that the evidence does not stop the ping: an_idle_stream_is_pinged_at_the_clamped_interval for the agent, an_idle_stream_pings_at_the_clamped_interval for the provider.
